title: Standardization of Stamp Paper Value for Regulatory Compliance
summary: The requirement for non-judicial stamp paper for undertakings has evolved from specific, lower-value mandates (150 BDT) to a standardized, higher-value requirement (300 BDT) across various customs and AEO compliance procedures. This reflects a shift toward uniform administrative documentation standards for legal undertakings and affidavits in customs-related applications.

evolution.scope: Expanded from specific industrial import undertakings to broader AEO and duty exemption compliance frameworks.

timeline.change: Initial requirement for 150 BDT non-judicial stamp paper for import undertakings.
Standardization of stamp paper value to 300 BDT for AEO certification affidavits.
Consolidation of the 300 BDT stamp paper requirement for general duty exemption undertakings.

Imported Machinery and Equipment: Imported machinery and equipment must be used exclusively by registered organizations involved in the manufacturing of seagoing vessels, inland cargo vessels, passenger vessels, or dredgers.
Importers are required to submit a formal undertaking on a non-judicial stamp paper as specified in the relevant appendix to the Commissioner of Customs.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs is the designated authority to whom the importer must submit a formal undertaking regarding the mandated use of imported machinery and equipment.

Authorized Economic Operator: Applicants for the Authorized Economic Operator certificate must submit a formal application in the prescribed format to the Director General.
The application process requires submitting a Self-Assessment Questionnaire, supporting documentation, and a sworn affidavit on a non-judicial stamp paper.

Applications are subject to a preliminary verification process, and failure to provide complete or accurate documentation within specified timelines will result in the application being processed further or rejected.
An application will be rejected if the applicant is not directly involved in customs processes or fails to rectify deficiencies within the stipulated timeframe.
Self-Assessment Questionnaire: Applicants must submit a completed Self-Assessment Questionnaire as part of the mandatory documentation required for the Authorized Economic Operator certification process.
Customs Authority: The designated Center is responsible for maintaining a register of applications, issuing acknowledgments of receipt, and conducting preliminary verification of submitted materials.
If an application is found to be incomplete, the center must notify the applicant within a set period to rectify the identified deficiencies.

Authorized Economic Operator: This entity acts as the recipient for formal applications submitted by entities seeking recognition as an Authorized Economic Operator.
Applicants must submit a formal application to receive recognition as an Authorized Economic Operator under the relevant governing rules.

The application process requires the submission of a sworn affidavit on non-judicial stamp paper and a completed Self-Assessment Questionnaire, supported by relevant institutional documentation and verified by management.
Self-Assessment Questionnaire: Applicants for AEO status are required to complete this questionnaire as part of their formal submission to the appropriate customs authority.
Business Identification Number: Applicants are required to provide their Business Identification Number as part of the detailed information disclosed in their formal application for AEO recognition.

Manufacturing Entities: Manufacturing entities are required to fulfill specific conditions and adhere to prescribed manufacturing processes as a prerequisite for claiming tax exemptions under this notification.

The application must be accompanied by supporting documentation and a formal undertaking on a non-judicial stamp paper of a specified value, ensuring compliance with the prescribed production conditions.
Tax Exemption: Eligibility for the tax exemption described in this order is strictly conditional upon the manufacturer adhering to the stipulated production terms and fulfilling all documentation requirements.

Pesticide Manufacturer: A pesticide manufacturing company must submit a certificate issued by an official from the Ministry of Agriculture, at least at the rank of Joint Secretary, to the Commissioner of Customs to confirm that imported goods will exclusively be used for pesticide production and packaging.
The company is required to provide a notarized undertaking on a non-judicial stamp paper affirming that imported materials will only be used for agricultural pesticide manufacturing.

In the event of an investigation or complaint by customs or local value-added tax authorities proving that materials were not used for the stated purpose, the manufacturer must pay all applicable duties and taxes on the imported goods.

Customs Duty: Manufacturers are liable to pay all applicable customs duties and other taxes if it is found that imported raw materials were not utilized for the production of agricultural pesticides.
Value Added Tax: Local authorities responsible for this tax may initiate investigations or complaints against pesticide manufacturers if imported goods are misused or diverted from agricultural pesticide production.
